BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head. Work only inside that

The supervisor independently confirmed every sub-finding below against the code
before filing this bead. They are real; do not re-litigate them. Verify the

=== FINDING 2 (material — contract semantics change). Fix this first. ===

P7 collapses two mutually exclusive executions into one fixture. Today:
`campaignRuleState.cases` is the bare array
`['without-active-ruling', 'with-active-ruling-supplied-by-eshyra-jhpt']`;
the single `expectedRouteClasses` entry unconditionally requires
`campaign-ruling`; `expectedAmbiguityState` declares a single `unresolved`
expectation; and `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` carries two cases. Those
cannot all describe one execution: with no active ruling there is no
`campaign-ruling` route by definition and the ambiguity stays unresolved; with
an active ruling that route exists and carries the supplied identity and
provenance. W8 measures preserved retrieval routes and campaign-rule/ruling
matches, so a generic harness cannot evaluate P7 without inventing P7-specific
semantics for the `cases` array — which defeats W7's purpose as the durable
diagnostic oracle.

REQUIRED SHAPE — make executions first-class and GENERIC, not P7-special.

Split `DiagnosticFixture` into scenario-level fields and a non-empty
`executions` list. Scenario-level (shared by every execution of the scenario):
`playerInput`, `campaignState`, `adventureState`, `mustIncludeTargets`,
`mayIncludeTargets`, `mustNotIncludeTargets`, `requiredRetainedFacts`,
`requiredRelationshipExpansion`, plus the metadata (`probeId`, `title`,
`verifiedAtCommit`, `gatingBlocker`, `boundedEvidenceStatement`).

Each `FixtureExecution` carries its own exact:
`executionId` (stable, kebab-case, unique within the fixture);
`campaignRuleState` (section-11 field 4, `ExplicitNone | Record`);
`expectedRouteClasses` (field 8);
`expectedAmbiguityState` (field 11);
`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` (field 12);
`expectedCapabilityStatus` (field 13);
`expectedDeterministicStateEffect`;
`oracleSignals` (an execution that consumes a supplied answer must label it
there, so the label travels with the execution that actually used it).

Every one of the thirteen section-11 fields must still be declared for every
execution — nested, not dropped. Eleven fixtures become a mechanical
single-execution wrap; only P7 gets two. Do NOT introduce a "primary execution
plus alternates" shape: uniformity is the point, because the reviewer's core
objection is that a generic downstream harness must be able to enumerate
executions without probe-specific knowledge.

P7's two executions, exactly:
  1. `without-active-ruling` — `campaignRuleState` explicitly none-active;
     routes for `magic-item:cube-of-force` are `direct-state-ref` and
     `capability-preflight` and MUST NOT include `campaign-ruling`; ambiguity
     `ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset` expected `unresolved`
     with both interpretation ids; `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` carries
     only the no-ruling case; `oracleSignals` is empty; capability status
     `blocked`.
  2. `with-active-ruling` — `campaignRuleState` carries the jhpt-supplied active
     ruling; routes include `campaign-ruling` alongside `direct-state-ref` and
     `capability-preflight`; ambiguity expected `resolved`; the ruling appears
     with identity, scope, and provenance, all owned by eshyra-jhpt and NOT
     invented here; `oracleSignals` carries the `jhpt-active-ruling` label;
     capability status is STILL `blocked`, because the readiness clauses are
     engine-pending independently of ruling resolution. That invariance is the
     whole point of the probe — state it explicitly in both executions.

This must remain a CONSUMER of the eshyra-jhpt oracle. Do not create a
discovery-owned ruling store, schema, resolver, or lifecycle (design §8.4).

Regression evidence required (new assertions in the currency test):
  - no-ruling execution → no `campaign-ruling` route anywhere in it, and the
    ambiguity is unresolved;
  - active-ruling execution → a `campaign-ruling` route is present, and the
    supplied ruling identity/provenance is present and labelled as an oracle
    signal;
  - capability readiness is `blocked` in BOTH executions.

=== FINDING 1 (enforcement hardening — must not change fixture meanings) ===

The currency gate is selectively fail-open. Five defects, all confirmed:

1. `stable-id.idKind` is not enforced semantically. `assertSelector`'s
   `operation` and `clause` branches are byte-identical and both call the
   recursive `findById`, which matches any `id`, `clauseId`, or `via`. An
   operation could vanish while the same string survived in another identifier
   role and the gate would stay green. Make each selector kind check the
   identifier role it actually names: an `operation` id must resolve as an
   operation id (including a state-machine `via` operation), a `clause` id must
   resolve as a clause id. Locate the real shapes in the pack
   (`data.mechanics.operations[].id`, `data.executionReadiness.clauses[].clauseId`,
   `data.mechanics.stateMachine.transitions[].via`) rather than pattern-matching
   any key named `id`.

2. P7's declared interpretation ids (`same-face-resets`,
   `different-face-only-resets`) are never verified against the pack. The
   currency test checks the ambiguity id only. Verify every declared
   `interpretationIds` entry resolves as an actual interpretation id on the
   named record's ambiguity, and verify the declared `expectedResolution` is
   consistent with the pack's `canonicalResolution` for the no-ruling execution
   (the pack has `canonicalResolution: null`).

3. `validateDiagnosticCorpus` requires each supplied route to point at a
   must-include target, but never requires that every unique must-include
   target HAS route coverage. A required candidate can silently lose field-8
   coverage. Require, per execution, that every unique must-include target
   reference appears in that execution's `expectedRouteClasses`.

4. P11 declares the synthetic add-on `rules:test-cursed-attunement-addon`
   version `1.0.0` overriding `magic-item:ring-of-protection`, but nothing binds
   that declaration to its real producer,
   `packages/core/test/support/cursedAttunementAddon.ts` (which defines
   `OVERRIDDEN_ITEM_REF = 'magic-item:ring-of-protection'` at :11, packId at :47,
   version at :51). The declaration is correct today but nothing keeps it
   current. The cited `campaignRulesStackParity.test.ts` proves the repaired
   resolver class with a DIFFERENT synthetic stack; it does not pin P11's
   identity. Bind P11's declared pack identity, version, and overridden record
   to the producer module — import from it and assert equality, or export the
   identities from the producer and have P11 consume them. Prefer consuming the
   producer's own exported constants so the two cannot drift.

5. There is no adversarial regression suite for the validator. The real corpus
   passing proves current examples, not that the gate rejects bad input. The
   `findingRegistry` pattern this work cites DOES include mutation-based
   rejection tests. Add adversarial mutation tests that deep-clone the real
   corpus, mutate one thing, and assert `validateDiagnosticCorpus` (or the
   currency assertions) reject it. Cover at minimum: wrong selector kind;
   a selector identity that no longer resolves; a must-include target with no
   route coverage; a missing probe; a duplicate probe id; a duplicate
   `executionId` within a fixture; an unanchored `exactSubstring` (the
   already-designed rejection); an unknown route class; an unlabelled oracle
   signal; and P7's no-ruling execution mutated to carry a `campaign-ruling`
   route.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Test-only. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes.
- Finding 1 is enforcement hardening: it must NOT change any fixture's meaning.
  If hardening a check makes a real fixture fail, the fixture's claim was wrong
  — fix the claim and say so in-band; do not weaken the check.
- No discovery implementation, no stage harness, no runtime integration.
- No fixture asserts a count of records; no coverage, readiness, or
  completeness figure over the corpus. Asserting twelve probes exist and that a
  fixture has N executions is contract structure, not a corpus count, and is
  fine.
- Every fixture keeps its bounded-evidence statement and `verifiedAtCommit`.
- P7 and P10 stay consumers of eshyra-jhpt; no second ruling model.
- Do not weaken or edit any existing test or audit expectation.
- Keep `VERIFIED_AT_COMMIT` current: if you re-verify at a newer merge base,
  update it and say why in the comment above it.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites
files). Expected: all non-skipped tests pass; documented skips are the live-API
integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests. The one acceptable Biome
finding is the pre-existing biome.json schema-version info (config 2.5.5,
installed 2.5.10).
acceptance_criteria: DiagnosticFixture carries a generic non-empty executions list; each FixtureExecution declares its own executionId, campaignRuleState, expectedRouteClasses, expectedAmbiguityState, expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState, expectedCapabilityStatus, expectedDeterministicStateEffect, and oracleSignals. P7 declares two executions (without-active-ruling, with-active-ruling) whose routes, ambiguity resolution, and ruling state differ correctly and whose capability status is blocked in both. Selector checking respects the selector discriminant semantically. P7 interpretation identities are verified against the pack. Every unique must-include target has route coverage per execution. P11's synthetic add-on identity is bound to cursedAttunementAddon.ts. Adversarial mutation tests reject wrong selector kind, unresolvable selector identity, missing route coverage, missing probe, duplicate probe id, duplicate executionId, unanchored exactSubstring, unknown route class, unlabelled oracle signal, and a campaign-ruling route in P7's no-ruling execution. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes. npm run verify:worktree passes.
